newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone, near high, slips on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone, near high, slips on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking pulled down shares of Vodafone Group Plc on Monday, after Britain's biggest mobile telephone company unveiled its new corporate identity, traders said.
By 1105 GMT, Vodafone was off 6p at 300p, after stopping just short of its lifetime high of 310p. The stock jumped 10 percent in the last two weeks alone.
"I don't think that (reorganisation) news had an impact," one trader said. "The stock was a good market on Thursday and Friday...and it reached a psychological level so there was some profit-taking."
Vodafone said it will reorganise its six service provider chains into three new businesses, which will eventually move to a unified billing system.
The changes will lead to around 300 jobs being phased out over the next 18 months and the company expects current year profits to be cut by 20 million stg.
It sees an improvement of 10 million pounds the following year and of 35 million by the third year.
After hitting a record high 504-1/2p, British Telecommunications Plc fell 8-1/2p to 493p. Cable and Wireless Plc lost 11p to 562-1/2p and Orange Plc traded 4-1/2p lower at 205-1/2p.
